alternate_names: Kali Bari Mandir, Industrial Area Phase II

history.summary: The Kalibari at Industrial Area Phase II is the principal Kali temple of Chandigarh's Bengali community and one of the city's oldest Durga Puja venues (it appears on 2025 lists of Chandigarh's top Durga Puja pandals). Worship centres on Goddess Kali, with a full-scale Durga Puja each Shardiya Navratri including cultural programmes and food fairs. The temple's founding year is not documented in the sources consulted; a '40th year / started 1983' Durga Puja claim found online refers to Noida's Kali Bari (NBCA), not Chandigarh's. Coordinates are a full-address geocode match. CSV state correction: Chandigarh is a Union Territory, not part of Haryana.

name: Chandigarh Kali Bari
town_description: Chandigarh is a Union Territory and India's first planned city, designed by Le Corbusier, serving as the shared capital of Punjab and Haryana. Laid out in self-contained sectors, it is known for the Rock Garden, Sukhna Lake and its modernist architecture.

travel.airport: Shaheed Bhagat Singh International Airport, Chandigarh (~12 km)
travel.road: City buses and auto-rickshaws; ~4 km from Sector 17 city centre

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Durga Puja (September-October) for the main festival
